title: Hashbank allocator and temperature-driven KV reclamation to reduce GPU fragmentation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The GPU KV cache continues to accumulate micro-fragmentation from heterogeneous request shapes (short and long sequences, embeddings, rerank use cases) and from opportunistic reallocations during continuous batching windows. Fragmentation manifests as unusable free holes, elevated memory waste, and increased GC/relocation pressure that spikes tail latency.

Proposal summary: Introduce a "Hashbank" allocation layer that segments KV storage into small banks by a stable hash of tokenized key prefixes, combined with a temperature-driven reclamation policy. Banks collect items with similar lifetime/size profiles; each bank tracks a lightweight temperature score (hot -> cold) based on access recency and eviction churn. Background micro-compaction preferentially targets cold banks during low-util windows, while hot banks stay read-optimized. The design includes hybrid free lists (per-stream small-bucket freelists + bank-level superblock management) to keep allocation fast for the continuous batching runtime.

Goals: Reduce fragmentation ratio by >=40% on mixed workloads, decrease background relocation IO, and keep 99th percentile generation latency within existing SLOs. Provide gradual rollout with safe fallbacks and fine-grained telemetry to verify unit economics (tokens/byte).
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end prototype reduces measured GPU memory waste (holes) by >=40% on the mixed-seq workload replay compared to baseline - measured via fragmentation_ratio metric.
Background micro-compaction events do not increase P99 request latency by more than 5% under 95th-percentile load profiles.
No data-loss or KV correctness regressions observed across canary runs; all canary runs auto-fallback on error to existing allocator.
New metrics and dashboards (fragmentation_ratio, bank_temperature, bank_rebalance_events) are available in the Console and alerts are defined for sustained degradation.
Documentation and runbook updated for on-call: how to interpret bank heatmaps and execute an emergency global compaction or rollback.
implementation_notes: Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INFR/pages/Hashbank+Allocator+Design (draft) - v0.1 attached; feedback requested from memory-team and serving-runtime.
Prototype path: implement Hashbank metadata and allocator in kv-store module (C++), micro-compactor as a light-weight CUDA kernel for bulk move of cold superblocks to reclaimed pools.
Simulator: extend existing kv-frag-sim harness to model bank heat decay, continuous batching alignment, and relocation cost; run 10k-sample traces from production workload replays.
Integration: expose bank-affinity hints to the continuous batching scheduler (batcher) so requests that map to same bank can be batched with KV locality in mind.
Memory layout: 64-bit aligned superblocks; small-entry bucket sizes: 64/128/256B. Metadata per entry reduced to 32-bit tag + 16-bit bank id to minimize overhead.
APIs: add metrics endpoints and an admin route to trigger per-bank compaction and to drain a bank for safe live migration.
Canary: phased rollout starting at 1% traffic, then 10%, 25%, 50% with automated rollback if fragmentation_ratio or P99 latency exceed thresholds.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Bank hash skew - some banks could become hotspots leading to overfill and eviction storms. Mitigation: use consistent rehashing with a lightweight remap table and probabilistic bank split when occupancy > threshold.

Risk: Micro-compactor contention with inference kernel causing latency spikes. Mitigation: compaction restricted to idle epochs measured by scheduler and capped CPU/GPU residency; preemptible kernels with immediate abort on latency tail signals.
Risk: Metadata blowup for very high QPS tenants. Mitigation: use compact tags and optional bank coalescing for small tenants; provide config flags per-customer (Dedicated/Private).
Risk: Complexity in batcher integration. Mitigation: fall back to existing behavior if bank-affinity hinting fails, and keep bank-affinity an opt-in optimizer which can be toggled per-route.
